title: Relative ampleness for schemes survives arbitrary base change
statement: Let $u$ be an arbitrary universe. Let $f:X\to T$ and $g:T'\to T$ be morphisms of schemes represented in the common universe $u$ (the universe is arbitrary) [def-pc-scheme], let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and put $X'=X\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to T'$. Suppose that for every affine open $V\subseteq T$, $L|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then for every affine open $V'\subseteq T'$, $(g'^*L)|_{(f')^{-1}(V')}$ is ample, where pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Tag 0893 (lemma-ample-base-change), with relative ampleness as in Tag 01VH (definition-relatively-ample). The affine-open hypothesis already implies quasi-compactness of f.

proof.text: For every affine open $V\subseteq T$, ampleness of $L|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ implies that $f^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact, by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. This is precisely the quasi-compactness condition on $f$ in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus $f$ is quasi-compact; no finite type hypothesis is being added.

source.place: Tag 01VH (definition-relatively-ample); the quasi-compactness already contained in absolute ampleness, Properties Tag 01PS.

proof.text: Let $L'=g'^*L$. The pullback is invertible by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. The projection $f':X'\to T'$ is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], applied to the quasi-compact morphism $f$ from Step 1 and the arbitrary base map $g$.

Choose affine open neighbourhoods $U'_i\subseteq T'$ covering $T'$, each mapping into some affine open $U_i\subseteq T$. Indeed, for a point $t'$ first choose an affine open $U_i$ containing $g(t')$, then an affine neighbourhood of $t'$ contained in the open $g^{-1}(U_i)$. This uses [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], first on $T$ and then on $T'$. Put $Z_i=f^{-1}(U_i)$ and $Z'_i=(f')^{-1}(U'_i)$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $Z'_i$ with $Z_i\times_{U_i}U'_i$: a map to either scheme is a pair of maps to $X$ and $U'_i$ whose composites to $T$ agree, and the map to $X$ factors through $Z_i$ because the second map lands over $U_i$. The projection $a_i:Z'_i\to Z_i$ is therefore the base change of $U'_i\to U_i$.

The morphism $U'_i\to U_i$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], since both its source and target are affine schemes. Its base change $a_i:Z'_i\to Z_i$ is affine by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. The hypothesis makes $L|_{Z_i}$ ample. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] gives that $a_i^*(L|_{Z_i})$ is ample on $Z'_i$. The restriction of $L'$ to $Z'_i$ is this very pullback: the two composites $Z'_i\to X$ agree, so functoriality of module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] identifies their pullbacks of $L$. Thus $L'|_{Z'_i}$ is ample for every $i$.

Apply [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-affine-cover] to $h=f'$, $N=L'$, and the affine open covering $\{U'_i\}$ from Step 3. Its quasi-compactness and invertibility hypotheses hold by Step 2, and ampleness over each member holds by Step 4. It follows that $L'|_{(f')^{-1}(V')}$ is ample for every affine open $V'\subseteq T'$, which is the assertion.

statement_change.what: The source quantifies over arbitrary schemes, while Mathlib’s Scheme category is homogeneous: a morphism X ⟶ T requires X and T (and hence the pullback data) to inhabit one Scheme.{u}. The corrected statement makes the arbitrary universe-polymorphic common-u encoding explicit; every triple of schemes can be represented in a common universe, so this is a size correction, not a geometric restriction.
